items.title: Why the CNS boom owes its success to breakthroughs in neurological pathologies
items.summary: Shifting emphasis from symptoms to biomarkers has bolstered sector confidence in emerging CNS therapies.

items.title: How Novartis' Double-Stacked Failures Reverberated Through Biopharma
items.summary: Novartis and Ionis' high-profile Lp(a) flop on Friday reverberated through biotech stocks on Tuesday, leading to a widespread drop.

items.title: GLP1 Drugs Work for Kids, Says Novo Nordisk. They Could Be Another Huge Market.
items.summary: Novo announced successful results from a Phase 3 study of its injectable GLP1 drug Wegovy in obese children aged six to 12.

items.title: Is AbbVie Stock Too Reliant On Skyrizi?
items.summary: AbbVie (ABBV) trades at $256.46, roughly 96% of its 52-week high, after returning 24.1% over the past twelve months against 19.7% for the S&P 500. That price buys a business where about a third of guided 2026 revenue comes from one drug. The market reads that concentration as strength. It is worth reading it the other way too.

items.title: Amgen Falls 10% as Novartis Trial Failure Clouds a Cholesterol Drug Class; NVS Stock Drops 14%
items.summary: Novartis just handed the entire Lp(a) drug class a failing grade, and Amgen is taking the worst of the punishment despite releasing promising trial results of its own on the very same morning.

items.title: Is Novo Nordisk Stock Still Too Cheap for Investors to Ignore?
items.summary: Shares of Novo Nordisk are trading 66% below their 2024 high, but is that enough to call them cheap? Maybe.

items.title: Stocks to Watch: Amgen, Qualcomm, Intel, Rigetti
items.summary: ↘️ Amgen (AMGN): Shares of the biotechnology company, a major contributor to the Dow, shed about 10%. The move came after the Swiss drugmaker Novartis (CH:NOVN) said late Friday that an experimental medicine failed to reduce cardiovascular risk in a late-stage clinical trial.

items.title: What Merck Stopped Saying About GARDASIL Should Change What You Watch
items.summary: Merck (MRK) has returned about 85% over the past year and at about $150 trades roughly 4% below its 52-week high. A year ago, management spent earnings calls managing fallout from a steep drop in GARDASIL sales. That problem has left the lead. What management opens with instead is a much larger claim, and it settles years from now.
